title: First Word Giving Receiving And Thanking Through Bismillah

questions.question: What should we say because all things bring Allah’s gifts to us by His command?
questions.answer: We should say, “In the Name of Allah.”

questions.question: How should we give and receive things?
questions.answer: We should give and receive for Allah’s sake and with His name.

questions.question: From what kind of people should we not take things?
questions.answer: From people who do not remember Allah when they give.

questions.question: In the passage, what are people compared to when they hand us blessings?
questions.answer: They are like helpers carrying a serving tray.

questions.question: Who is the real owner of the blessings?
questions.answer: Allah.

questions.question: What three things does Allah want from us in return for His gifts?
questions.answer: Remembering Him, thanking Him, and thinking deeply.

questions.question: What is one way to remember Allah before using a blessing?
questions.answer: To begin with Allah’s name.

questions.question: What is one way to thank Allah after receiving a blessing?
questions.answer: To praise Him.

questions.question: What does it mean to reflect on blessings?
questions.answer: It means to notice them, think about them, and see them as gifts from Allah.

questions.question: Why is it wrong to love only the thing or person that seems to give the blessing?
questions.answer: Because that forgets Allah, who truly gives it.

questions.question: What example shows this mistake in the passage?
questions.answer: Honoring the one who delivers a king’s gift but ignoring the king.

questions.question: What final advice is given to the nafs?
questions.answer: To start, take, give, and act in Allah’s name.

questions.question: What is the main lesson of this passage?
questions.answer: We should remember Allah when we use His blessings.

questions.question: Why should people say Allah’s name too?
questions.answer: Because all things serve by Allah’s command and bring His gifts.

questions.question: When we pay a person for something, does that mean the person is the true giver?
questions.answer: No. The person is only a means, and Allah is the true giver.

questions.question: What picture is used for people who pass blessings to us?
questions.answer: They are pictured like someone carrying food to others.

questions.question: What does Allah ask from us instead of money for His blessings?
questions.answer: He asks for remembrance, thanks, and reflection.

questions.question: What does remembrance mean here?
questions.answer: It means turning to Allah and starting with His name.

questions.question: What does thanks mean here?
questions.answer: It means praising Allah after receiving His gift.

questions.question: What does reflection help us understand about blessings?
questions.answer: That they are amazing gifts made by Allah’s power and mercy.

questions.question: If someone enjoys a blessing but forgets Allah, what mistake is that person making?
questions.answer: The person is caring about the gift but forgetting the real Giver.

questions.question: Why is that called foolish in the passage?
questions.answer: Because it is silly to honor the messenger and ignore the one who sent the gift.

questions.question: What should a person do to avoid that foolishness?
questions.answer: Use Allah’s name when giving, taking, beginning, and acting.

questions.question: According to the passage, who truly gives us the good things we enjoy?
questions.answer: Allah truly gives them.

questions.question: What should we do before we begin something good?
questions.answer: Say Allah’s name.

questions.question: What should we do after receiving a blessing?
questions.answer: Thank Allah.

questions.question: Besides remembering and thanking, what is the third thing we should do?
questions.answer: Think carefully about the blessing.

questions.question: What should we think about when we reflect on a blessing?
questions.answer: That it is precious and comes from Allah’s mercy and power.

questions.question: Why should we not depend only on people for blessings?
questions.answer: Because people are not the real owners of them.

questions.question: What kind of people are we warned not to take from?
questions.answer: People who give without remembering Allah.

questions.question: In the question inside the passage, what is being asked about Allah?
questions.answer: What He wants from us for His gifts.

questions.question: Does Allah want payment like money for His blessings?
questions.answer: No. He wants remembrance, thanks, and reflection.

questions.question: What lesson comes from the example of a king’s gift?
questions.answer: We should honor the real giver more than the one who brings it.

questions.question: If someone praises only the created thing and forgets Allah, what are they missing?
questions.answer: They are missing the truth that Allah is the source of the blessing.

questions.question: What is the short ending advice to the nafs?
questions.answer: Live and act with Allah’s name.

questions.question: What do all things do with Allah’s blessings, according to the passage?
questions.answer: They bring them to us by Allah’s command.

questions.question: Since that is true, what should we also do?
questions.answer: We should say Allah’s name.

questions.question: What two actions are named together in the passage about daily life?
questions.answer: Giving and taking.

questions.question: How should those two actions be done?
questions.answer: They should be done in Allah’s name.

questions.question: What warning is given about some people?
questions.answer: Some people forget Allah when they give.

questions.question: Why should a believer be careful about taking from such people?
questions.answer: Because giving should be connected to remembering Allah.

questions.question: What question is raised about the “price” of blessings?
questions.answer: It asks what Allah wants from us in return.

questions.question: Name the first of the three things Allah wants.
questions.answer: Remembering Him.

questions.question: Name the second of the three things Allah wants.
questions.answer: Thanking Him.

questions.question: Name the third of the three things Allah wants.
questions.answer: Reflecting on His gifts.

questions.question: What is one simple sign of remembrance at the start of something?
questions.answer: Beginning with Allah’s name.

questions.question: What is one simple sign of thanks at the end?
questions.answer: Saying praise to Allah.

questions.question: Why is reflection important, not just words?
questions.answer: Because it helps us understand that blessings are wonderful gifts from Allah.

questions.question: What mistake does the passage compare to honoring a delivery person more than a king?
questions.answer: Loving the seen source of a blessing more than Allah.

questions.question: What should a Muslim remember when receiving any blessing?
questions.answer: That it comes truly from Allah.

questions.question: What does the passage teach us to say at the beginning of something?
questions.answer: Allah’s name.

questions.question: What does it teach us to say at the end of enjoying a blessing?
questions.answer: Words of praise to Allah.

questions.question: What are the three responses Allah wants from us?
questions.answer: Remembrance, thanks, and reflection.

questions.question: Which one of the three means using your mind to notice Allah’s gifts?
questions.answer: Reflection.

questions.question: Which one of the three means showing gratefulness?
questions.answer: Thanks.

questions.question: Which one of the three means keeping Allah in mind from the start?
questions.answer: Remembrance.

questions.question: What example from the passage teaches that a messenger is not the real owner?
questions.answer: A person bringing a ruler’s gift is not the ruler.

questions.question: If a child loves the gift but forgets who sent it, what is the problem?
questions.answer: The child is forgetting the true giver.

questions.question: Why are blessings called very valuable in the passage?
questions.answer: Because they are special gifts from Allah’s mercy.

questions.question: What four actions are told to be done in Allah’s name at the end of the passage?
questions.answer: Giving, taking, beginning, and acting.

questions.question: What is one big idea in this passage about blessings?
questions.answer: Blessings should lead us to Allah.

questions.question: What should come with our giving?
questions.answer: Allah’s name.

questions.question: What should come with our taking?
questions.answer: Allah’s name.

questions.question: Why are human givers not the final source of blessings?
questions.answer: Because Allah is the true owner and giver.

questions.question: What job are people compared to when they pass blessings to others?
questions.answer: They are compared to carriers bringing something from the owner.

questions.question: What does Allah ask back from us for His many gifts?
questions.answer: Remembrance, thanks, and reflection.

questions.question: How can a child show remembrance in a simple way?
questions.answer: By starting with Allah’s name.

questions.question: How can a child show thanks in a simple way?
questions.answer: By praising Allah.

questions.question: How can a child show reflection in a simple way?
questions.answer: By thinking, “This beautiful gift came from Allah.”

questions.question: What foolish mistake does the passage warn against?
questions.answer: Forgetting Allah and only noticing the thing or person in front of us.

questions.question: What comparison makes that warning easy to understand?
questions.answer: It is like thanking the one who carries a gift but ignoring the one who sent it.

questions.question: What is the last instruction given to the nafs?
questions.answer: To do everything in Allah’s name.
